title: Sluice-based turn groomer for steady streaming batches
creator: Aisha Rao
description: Summary: Implement a novel 'sluice' turn grooming layer that continuously groups incoming streaming chat requests into stable micro-batches while proactively managing KV cache placement and per-GPU slab reservations. The goal is to reduce p99 tail for streaming completions while increasing steady-state throughput and lowering transient GPU memory spikes.
background_and_motivation: Current streaming batchers prioritize latency-first grouping and enforce rigid turn boundaries which leads to frequent KV thrash and uneven GPU slab usage (observed OOM spikes during bursty multi-turn sessions). We need a continuous, telemetry-driven bundling strategy that smooths KV fragments across micro-batches, prefetches hot KV slots, and opportunistically co-locates short-turn tails to boost packing efficiency without increasing worst-case latency significantly.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Proto-layer deployed behind feature flag on a subset of traffic (10% internal). 2) End-to-end telemetry demonstrates >=10% improvement in aggregate tokens/sec on selected 4k-context models and <=5ms regression to median generation latency. 3) p99 streaming token latency reduced by >=8% in our benchmark harness. 4) No GPU OOM incidents in the canary window. 5) Automated toggles allow roll back by traffic group.
design_summary:
Key components:
- Sluice buckets: time-decayed bins that group requests by recent activity, estimated remaining length, and KV heat score. Each bucket forms micro-batches up to a soft token budget.
- KV fragment smoothing: assign KV slots to slab slices and attempt to co-locate requests with overlapping prefixes or high KV reuse to reduce KV materialization cost.
- Telemetry-driven budgets: per-GPU live metrics (free slab bytes, active KV refs, prefetch latency) drive per-bucket token ceilings and slab reservations.
- Early-finish packing: if a request signals a short-turn (based on token estimate or eos seen) it can be pulled forward into the next micro-batch to avoid wait amplification.
- Graceful fallback: if prefetch misses or slab pressure is high, sluice drops to conservative pack mode (single-request priority) and emits debug events for SRE.
algorithm_sketch: 1) On request arrival compute a bucket key: hash(user_session_id, recent-turn-hash, token_estimate_range). 2) Lookup the pool for the target GPU(s) and check live slab_headroom. 3) If slab_headroom >= bucket_min_reserve && average_bucket_wait < target_latency_budget then enqueue into the bucket. 4) Periodically (every 6ms) drain buckets producing micro-batches with token ceilings derived from telemetry smoothing (EWMA). 5) For each micro-batch, prefetch KV slots into reserved slab slices asynchronously and mark batch as 'prefetch-fulfilled' before dispatch. 6) If prefetch latency exceeds threshold, mark batch for partial-eviction and downgrade to streaming-first path.
tradeoffs_and_open_questions:
- Prefetch helps throughput but increases transient memory; what headroom threshold accurately balances throughput vs OOM risk?
- How aggressive should short-turn pulling be for low-latency conversational agents vs long-form completions?
- Interaction with autoscaler: sluice's slab reservations may lead to underutilized GPUs during very low load; need autoscaler integration to release reserves.
- Measuring customer-visible quality: co-locating prefixes might change caching behavior and marginally affect generation determinism; need eval prompts.
prototype_results:
Canary (internal traffic subset) summary:
- Throughput: +18% tokens/sec (4k-ctx T=1.3B model) under synthetic mixing workload.
- p99 streaming token latency: -12% relative to baseline (latency-first batcher).
- GPU memory tail: max slab used reduced by 9% in steady state; transient peaks reduced but one prefetch misprediction caused a spike (investigating).
- CPU overhead: +4% scheduler cycles due to sluice maintenance ticks.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1: core sluice bucket scheduler + telemetry hooks + feature flag (2 sprints). Phase 2: KV prefetch integration and slab reservation APIs (1 sprint). Phase 3: autoscaler handoff + rollout and safety gates (1 sprint). Phase 4: incremental rollout to external canary customers and postmortem.
Deliverables: design doc, unit + integration tests, observability dashboards, rollback playbook.
observability_and_metrics:
Add the following metrics and dashboards:
- sluice.bucket.count, sluice.bucket.wait_ms_p50/p95/p99
- sluice.prefetch.hit_rate, sluice.prefetch_latency_ms_p50/p95/p99
- gpu.slab.headroom_bytes per GPU, gpu.slab.reservations_count
- batcher.microbatch.token_count distribution
- rollback_trigger_events and sluice.fallback_rate
Include trace snippets linking request->bucket->prefetch events for live debugging.
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: prefetch mispredictions causing OOM. Mitigation: conservative initial reserve (5% slab), live OOM guard that immediately disables sluice per-pool, and circuit break with exponential backoff for reenable.
Risk: increased scheduler overhead. Mitigation: use adaptive tick interval and offload heavy computations to async worker pool.
